title: The observation request
description: Asks the running sketch to be observed. The writer places this atomically by way of a temporary file, and id changes with every request (ADR-0018 decision 3). With count at 2 or more, shots are taken in succession without stopping the frame loop, and the catalogue is written last. **A request whose id can be read is always answered**: one that cannot be read otherwise (a scale, count or every of the wrong type, such as "0.5" or true) takes no shot, the previous products are cleared, and the reply carries the reason in warnings. A request whose id cannot be read (missing, not a string, or text that is not JSON) gets no reply, and a request whose id was already answered is not processed again (see id). **A key this version does not read never fails the request**, so a writer can add keys without breaking an older sketch; the shot is taken without it and the reply's warnings name the key (a misspelt scale, as in sacle, is not read as scale).

id.description: This request's identifier. The reply echoes it back. A request with an id already seen is not processed again, even after the sketch relaunches: the answer left in the reply is the record. Do not reuse an id while the facet remains. **This includes a request that could not be read**: once it is answered, fixing it and placing it again under the same id is not processed — place the fixed request with a new id.

scale.description: How far to scale the written image down (1 = full size). 1 when omitted, and null reads as omitted. A scale outside this range is never replaced in silence: above 1, or at or below 0, the image is written at full size and the reply's warnings say so.

count.description: How many shots to take. 1 when omitted, and null reads as omitted. Asking outside the range is never clamped in silence: the count used, and whether the ceiling or the floor cut it, appear in the reply's warnings.

every.description: Take a shot every this many frames. Every frame when omitted, and null reads as omitted. Asking outside the range is never clamped in silence, as with count. **Counted in frames rather than seconds**, so the shots follow the frames the sketch actually draws. The sketch being observed runs on the wall clock unless it chose `clock: .frames`, and writing the images makes frames heavier, so **the shots are not evenly spaced in time** — lay the series out by each entry's `time` in the catalogue (frames), rather than assuming an even gap. For motion with evenly spaced times, write it with `mokume render` instead: it runs the sketch at a fixed frame rate and writes every frame, so nothing needs laying out again.

time.description: Draw exactly one frame at these seconds before taking it. Rounded to Float. deltaTime is zero and frameCount advances once. The picture is shown and draw side effects remain; this is not a rewind. Only count=1 and every=1 are allowed. noLoop stays stopped; external pause and recording refuse the request. Omit it, or write null, to observe normally. Check appliedTime and frames[0].time in the reply; older sketches may ignore this key.
